publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
bibl.publisher: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: Here we show that scaling up language models greatly improves task-agnostic, few-shot performance, sometimes even reaching competitiveness with prior state-of-the-art finetuning approaches.

span.label: in-context (few-shot) learning in large language models
span.quote: Recent work [RWC+19] attempts to do this via what we call “in-context learning”, using the text input of a pretrained language model as a form of task specification: the model is conditioned on a natural language instruction and/or a few demonstrations of the task and is then expected to complete further instances of the task simply by predicting what comes next.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: In this paper, we test this hypothesis by training a 175 billion parameter autoregressive language model, which we call GPT-3, and measuring its in-context learning abilities.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: in-context (few-shot) learning: a large pretrained language model performs a new task from a few demonstrations placed in its prompt, with no gradient updates - an ability that emerges from scale
span.quote: GPT-3 is applied without any gradient updates or fine-tuning, with tasks and few-shot demonstrations specified purely via text interaction with the model

span.label: one-shot/zero-shot are fairer human comparisons and remain targets for future work
span.note: what this limits: the human-comparison framing: one-shot and zero-shot are the fairer comparisons and remain IMPORTANT TARGETS FOR FUTURE WORK, not settled here
span.quote: important targets for future work

span.label: Text synthesis still degrades over long passages: repetition, loss of coherence, self-contradiction, non-sequiturs.
span.note: what this limits: the text-synthesis results specifically: GPT-3 SAMPLES STILL SOMETIMES REPEAT THEMSELVES SEMANTICALLY AT THE DOCUMENT LEVEL, START TO LOSE COHERENCE over long passages
span.quote: On text synthesis, although the overall quality is high, GPT-3 samples still sometimes repeat themselves semantically at the document level, start to lose coherence over sufficiently long passages, contradict themselves, and occasionally contain non-sequitur sentences or paragraphs.

span.label: The study covers only autoregressive models; no bidirectional architectures or denoising objectives were tested.
span.note: what this limits: the scope of every architectural conclusion: OUR EXPERIMENTS DO NOT INCLUDE ANY BIDIRECTIONAL ARCHITECTURES OR OTHER TRAINING OBJECTIVES SUCH AS DENOISING
span.quote: As a result our experiments do not include any bidirectional architectures or other training objectives such as denoising.

span.label: Pre-training sample efficiency is poor compared with human learning.
span.note: what this limits: any comparison with human learning: POOR SAMPLE EFFICIENCY DURING PRE-TRAINING is shared by language models broadly
span.quote: Another limitation broadly shared by language models is poor sample efficiency during pre-training.

span.label: It is unclear whether few-shot learning genuinely learns new tasks at inference time or merely recognises tasks seen in training.
span.note: what this limits: the interpretation of few-shot learning itself: AMBIGUITY ABOUT WHETHER FEW-SHOT LEARNING ACTUALLY LEARNS NEW TASKS FROM SCRATCH AT INFERENCE time, or recognises tasks seen in training
span.quote: A limitation, or at least uncertainty, associated with few-shot learning in GPT-3 is ambiguity about whether few-shot learning actually learns new tasks “from scratch” at inference time, or if it simply recognizes and identifies tasks that it has learned during training.

span.label: The model is uninterpretable, poorly calibrated on novel inputs, and retains its training data's biases.
span.note: what this limits: any deployment or calibration use: ITS DECISIONS ARE NOT EASILY INTERPRETABLE, IT IS NOT NECESSARILY WELL-CALIBRATED, and it retains its training data's biases
span.quote: Finally, GPT-3 shares some limitations common to most deep learning systems – its decisions are not easily interpretable, it is not necessarily well-calibrated in its predictions on novel inputs as observed by the much higher variance in performance than humans on standard benchmarks, and it retains the biases of the data it has been trained on.

span.label: A filtering bug left benchmark data in the training set and retraining was unaffordable.
span.note: what this limits: every benchmark number in the paper: A BUG IN THE FILTERING CAUSED US TO IGNORE SOME OVERLAPS, AND DUE TO THE COST OF TRAINING IT WAS NOT FEASIBLE TO RETRAIN THE MODEL - the contamination is known and was left in
span.quote: Unfortunately, a bug in the filtering caused us to ignore some overlaps, and due to the cost of training it was not feasible to retrain the model.

span.label: The contamination analysis cannot guarantee the 'clean' subsets are distributionally comparable to the full benchmarks.
span.note: what this limits: the contamination correction specifically: WE CANNOT BE SURE THAT THE CLEAN SUBSET IS DRAWN FROM THE SAME DISTRIBUTION AS THE ORIGINAL DATASET - the remedy is unvalidated
span.quote: An important limitation of our contamination analysis is that we cannot be sure that the clean subset is drawn from the same distribution as the original dataset.

span.label: The bias analysis is preliminary and incomplete even for gender, race and religion.
span.note: what this limits: the bias findings only: THIS IS A PRELIMINARY ANALYSIS AND DOES NOT REFLECT ALL OF THE MODEL'S BIASES EVEN WITHIN THE STUDIED CATEGORIES
span.quote: This is a preliminary analysis and does not reflect all of the model’s biases even within the studied categories.

span.label: SAT analogy problems - 374 of them, an instrument built to test American secondary-school pupils - collected and used as a few-shot benchmark for a language model
span.quote: 3.9.3 SAT Analogies To test GPT-3 on another task that is somewhat unusual relative to the typical distribution of text, we collected a set of 374 “SAT analogy” problems [TLBS03].

span.label: a parallel experiment in the same format using intentionally BAD model-generated articles
span.note: eliminates: inattentive or low-effort raters as the explanation of the headline result - if participants cannot detect deliberately bad output either, their failure to detect good output means nothing
span.quote: However, we also ran an experiment to control for participant effort and attention that followed the same format but involved intentionally bad model generated articles.

span.label: in-context learning
span.quote: We use the term “in-context learning” to describe the inner loop of this process, which occurs within the forward-pass upon each sequence.

span.label: few-shot learning
span.quote: Few-Shot (FS) is the term we will use in this work to refer to the setting where the model is given a few demonstrations of the task at inference time as conditioning [RWC+19], but no weight updates are allowed.

span.label: fine-tuning
span.quote: In this work we do not fine-tune GPT-3 because our focus is on task-agnostic performance, but GPT-3 can be fine-tuned in principle and this is a promising direction for future work. • Few-Shot (FS) is the term we will use in this work to refer to the setting where the model is given a few demonstrations of the task at inference time as conditioning [RWC+19], but no weight updates are allowed.

span.label: few-shot - K demonstrations supplied at inference time as conditioning, with no weight updates; K typically 10 to 100
span.quote: Few-Shot (FS) is the term we will use in this work to refer to the setting where the model is given a few demonstrations of the task at inference time as conditioning [RWC+19], but no weight updates are allowed.

span.label: one-shot - exactly one demonstration, distinguished not on performance grounds but because it matches how tasks are communicated to people
span.quote: One-Shot (1S) is the same as few-shot except that only one demonstration is allowed, in addition to a natural language description of the task, as shown in Figure 1. The reason to distinguish one-shot from few-shot and zero-shot (below) is that it most closely matches the way in which some tasks are communicated to humans.

span.label: zero-shot - no demonstrations at all, only a natural language instruction; described as the most convenient and the most challenging setting
span.quote: Zero-Shot (0S) is the same as one-shot except that no demonstrations are allowed, and the model is only given a natural language instruction describing the task. This method provides maximum convenience, potential for robustness, and avoidance of spurious correlations (unless they occur very broadly across the large corpus of pre-training data), but is also the most challenging setting.

span.label: in-context learning - a term the authors introduce for the inner loop that occurs within a single forward pass, not for weight change
span.quote: We use the term “in-context learning” to describe the inner loop of this process, which occurs within the forward-pass upon each sequence.

span.label: contradicts → the fine-tuning paradigm (task-specific fine-tuning)
span.quote: GPT-3 is applied without any gradient updates or fine-tuning

span.label: builds-on → GPT-2 [RWC+19] and the Sparse Transformer [CGRS19]
span.quote: We use the same model and architecture as GPT-2 [RWC+19], including the modified initialization, pre-normalization, and reversible tokenization described therein, with the exception that we use alternating dense and locally banded sparse attention patterns in the layers of the transformer, similar to the Sparse Transformer [CGRS19].

span.label: extends → the in-context learning of [RWC+19] (GPT-2)
span.quote: Our use of in-context learning is also similar to [RWC+19], but in this work we systematically explore different settings for learning within the context.

span.label: contradicts → [BHT+20]'s argument that continuing to expand hardware and data sizes is not the path forward
span.quote: We find that path is still promising and in a zero-shot setting GPT-3 achieves 76% on LAMBADA, a gain of 8% over the previous state of the art.

span.label: replicates → the power-law scaling of language-model loss reported by [KMH+20]
span.quote: The power-law behavior observed in [KMH+20] continues for an additional two orders of magnitude with only small deviations from the predicted curve.

span.label: extends → the closed-book QA result of [RRS20]
span.quote: Their work suggests that even higher-capacity models could perform even better and we test this hypothesis with GPT-3.

span.label: few-shot learning —distinct-from→ fine-tuning
span.quote: In this work we do not fine-tune GPT-3 because our focus is on task-agnostic performance, but GPT-3 can be fine-tuned in principle and this is a promising direction for future work. • Few-Shot (FS) is the term we will use in this work to refer to the setting where the model is given a few demonstrations of the task at inference time as conditioning [RWC+19], but no weight updates are allowed.
